text:
Construction builds by area. Commissioning starts by system. The gap between the two is where many EPC projects lose their last six months.

Engineering issues isometrics by area. Construction erects by area. Progress is reported by area. Everyone sees green.

Then, at around 80 %, commissioning asks for the first priority system. The loop runs through four areas. Each area is 90 % complete. The loop is not ready for test, because the 10 % left in each area happens to be on it.

A progress report gives you the numbers. It does not show you where the remaining work is.

So I put the actual progress on the 3D model. Every spool takes its status from the site lists: not received, received, doubled at ground, erected, fit-up done, welded. The video shows the demo version on fictional data, in under a minute:

• Pick a unit and the balance is visible at a glance.
• Show only the MC-01 loop and everything else goes pale. That is the degreasing scope, in 3D.
• Rank test packs by how much is already welded, then light one up: the least work that releases a hydrotest, and exactly where it is.
• Press Play and the P6 plan runs forward to MC-01, MC-02 and completion.

Management sees the strategy. A supervisor sees which spools to erect tomorrow. Nobody has to open P6.

Area progress tells you how much is done. System progress tells you when you can start up.

When did your current project fix its test-pack boundaries: before construction, during, or when commissioning asked for them?
